answer: Use the `template` commands. A template entry is an object/attribute pair plus the value to be used as the default for that attribute: `add template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> object <value> attribute <value> value <value> [sequence-id <value>] [label <value>] [condition <value>]`, with matching `set`, `show template-<group>/<name> [sequence-id] [object] [attribute] [value] [label] [condition]` and `delete`. object is the object name (e.g. odu), attribute the attribute name (e.g. admin-state), value is mandatory (e.g. lock); label and condition (e.g. service-type=OTU4) are optional. sequence-id is a Number in range 1..65535 and defines the processing order, lower ids first. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add template-1/FansInMaintenance object card attribute admin-state value maintenance condition card-type=FAN. Entries are pushed with apply-template.

No. A template-group is a configuration group holding a list of template entries, created with `add template-group-<name> [enabled <value>] [label <value>]`. The enabled attribute takes true or false, and its default is true only if there is no other template-group enabled. So the first group you add comes up enabled by itself, but with one already enabled a new group does not default to enabled; only one enabled group is in effect. Check with `show template-group-<name> [enabled] [label]` and remove with `delete template-group-<name>`. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add template-group-1.

`show templates`. It shows the configuration that defines the data model for system templates, i.e. the overall templates view on the node. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. To drill down, use `show template-group-<name> [enabled] [label]` for a single template group and `show template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> [sequence-id] [object] [attribute] [value] [label] [condition]` for an individual template entry.

No. `unlock` releases a database previously locked with the `lock` command, but only the session that performed the lock can trigger the unlock. If a session tries to unlock a non-locked database, or a database that was locked by another session, the unlock command will fail. A lock is automatically released if the session that performed the lock is closed, so once the colleague's session drops the database frees itself. After the unlock, any session is able to perform configurations and to take a new lock. Syntax: `unlock [-h]`, where -h displays help for this command. Access mode: Operational Mode.

Yes. `validate candidate <candidate> command <string>` validates the contents of the specified configuration, that is, any CLI command(s) used to edit a configuration datastore by creating, deleting, merging or replacing content, without applying them. candidate is the candidate datastore used as target for validation; command is the command text to validate. If the command is validated, the reply is 'OK'; otherwise the command fails. Multiple CLI commands can be provided in one invocation if separated with ';'. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: validate 'set ne altitude 600'.

A maximum of 7 rounds. Use `add additional-key-exchange-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<additional-key-exchange-id> dh-group <value>` (set/show/delete on the same key), where additional-key-exchange-id is 1..7 and number is the IKE SA proposal number. You must choose a unique key-exchange algorithm for each round, and the rounds must be configured in the same order on both IKE peers; if the configuration does not match, an IKE-CONFIG-MISMATCH alarm is raised. Configuring additional-key-exchange is optional and causes the IKE session to go down immediately and renegotiate the new proposal. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768, ml-kem-1024. Port level (CHILD-SA) key exchange is derived from IKE. For PQC safety configure PPK or at least one post-quantum algorithm; ml-kem-1024 is recommended as the strongest.

`show data-path-encryption`. This command shows the datapath encryption attributes. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The related global L1 encryption policy is held on the ikev2 object: `show ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match]`, and per-card IKE state is under `show ikev2-local-instance-<name>` with scope data-path-encryption.

Use `add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>` for a Child SA proposal, or `add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>` for the IKE SA proposal; only add, show and delete exist (all values are part of the key). algorithm: null, aes-gcm-8, aes-gcm-12, aes-gcm-16, aes-ctr, aes-cbc, aes-ccm-8, aes-ccm-12, aes-ccm-16, chacha20-poly1305. key-length: none, key-length-128, key-length-192, key-length-256, default none. number is the proposal number for the IKE SA, range 1..max. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add encryption-algorithm-ipsec/GX2/1/aes-gcm-8/key-length-192.

On `add ike-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>` both integrity-algorithm and dh-group are required; prf is optional. integrity-algorithm: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. dh-group: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512. prf: hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-384, hmac-sha2-512, hmac-sha1. number is the proposal number for the IKE SA, range 1..max. protocol-id is read-only, always IKE, and appears in show only. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add ike-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/1 dh-group dhe-2048 prf hmac-sha2-256 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-384-192.

The top-level ikev2 object carries exactly one attribute, data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match: `set ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match <value>]` and `show ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match]`. It is a global, L1 encryption-specific policy indicating whether the NE must validate the certificate Subject Alternate Name to match the IKE ID (OPT-IN) or not (OPT-OUT). Permitted values are match and ignore; no default is stated. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set ikev2 data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match match.

Read host-card-encryption-capability on the instance: `show ikev2-local-instance-<name> [host-card-encryption-capability] [scope] [host-card] [local-address-assignment-method] [local-address] ...`. It indicates whether the card on which this IKEv2 local instance is running supports encryption; values yes, no, unknown, default unknown. host-card is a reference to the service card the instance runs on. The local IKE address is picked by local-address-assignment-method, values auto or manual with default auto (show only). local-address is the local IPv4 address for the IKEv2 channel with prefix-length 32, settable, default 0.0.0.0. scope takes data-path-encryption, management-ipsec, local-address, local-address-assignment-method. Other settables: label, admin-state (lock, maintenance, unlock; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default Inhibited). Example: set ikev2-local-instance-1-3 local-address 1.1.180.132.

On ikev2-peer, re-key-frequency is the re-key frequency for the IKE SA with the far-end peer, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 28800; re-auth-frequency is the re-authentication frequency, range 3600..604800 seconds, default 43200. Range and default values may be context-specific. The stated rule is that re-key-frequency and re-auth-frequency must not be multiples of each other, and they must differ by a few minutes to ensure a significant interval between re-authentication and re-keying. Related failure handling: re-key-fail-policy (kill traffic, continue traffic; default continue-traffic) with re-key-traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s, default 0, and re-auth-fail-policy with re-auth-traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s, default 0. Set them with `set ikev2-peer-<local-instance>/<peer> re-key-frequency <value> re-auth-frequency <value>`.

Use `add ipsec-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number> dh-group <value> [integrity-algorithm <value>]`. dh-group is required, integrity-algorithm is optional. dh-group: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448. integrity-algorithm: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. number is the proposal number, 1..max. protocol-id is read-only and always ESP, and esn (Extended Sequence Number support) is read-only with value esn; both appear only in show. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add ipsec-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/dns/1 dh-group dhe-3072 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512-256.

Yes. `add ipsec-sa-re-key-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name> [frequency <value>] [bytes <value>] [packets <value>]` (also set/show/delete) sets the re-key trigger for the IPsec child SA with the far-end peer. frequency is time based, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 14400. bytes re-keys on the amount of bytes transmitted, range 1048576..max, default 1073741824. packets re-keys on the amount of packets transmitted, either disabled or a number in range 1..9223372036854775808, default disabled. So volume based re-keying on bytes is on by default at 1 GB, while packet based re-keying is off until you set it. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The action attribute of ipsec-spd-entry indicates the IPsec treatment given to matching IP datagrams: protect, bypass or discard, default protect. And yes, it tunnels by default: mode is tunnel or transport with default tunnel. Syntax: `add ipsec-spd-entry-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name> priority <value> [description <value>] [action <value>] [ipsec-protocol <value>] [mode <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [esn <value>] [anti-replay-window <value>] [dynamic-ts <value>]`. priority is mandatory (uint8) and gives precedence between SPD entries. ipsec-protocol is ESP. esn true/false, default true. anti-replay-window applies when action=protect, range 32..1024, default 64. dynamic-ts disabled/enabled, default disabled. alarm-report-control allowed/inhibited, default allowed. Example: add ipsec-spd-entry-ipsec/GX2/dns priority 1 action protect.

Create a traffic selector under the SPD entry and hang the address and port ranges off it. `add ipsec-traffic-selector-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name> [next-layer-protocol <value>]`; next-layer-protocol is the inner (upper layer) protocol taken from the IPv4 protocol or IPv6 next header field, with values any (value 0), opaque (value 255) or a number in range 0-255, default any. The selector name is a string of length 1..64, pattern ([A-Za-z0-9 \-.,]*). The addresses and ports themselves are added as children of the selector: local-subnet and remote-subnet for the prefixes, local-ports and remote-ports for the port ranges. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add ipsec-traffic-selector-ipsec/GX2/Radius/ts1 next-layer-protocol 17.

Because start and stop are part of the instance identifier, not editable attributes. The AID is local-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>, and only add, show and delete are defined; there is no set. To change a range, delete the existing entry and add the new one. start takes all, opaque or a port number; stop is a port-number and defaults to 0 if not set, but 0 is only accepted when start is all or opaque. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Examples: add local-ports-ipsec/GX2/tacacs/ts1/all and, for a single port, add local-ports-ipsec/GX1/dns/ts1/53/53.

Add it under the traffic selector: `add local-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>`, with matching show and delete forms. prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, and broadcast for IPv4 only) and is part of the key, so there is no set command; to change it, delete and re-add. The parent names are the local instance name and peer name (string 1..64, pattern ([A-Za-z0-9 \-.,]*)), the SPD entry name (string 1..32) and the traffic selector name (string 1..64). Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add local-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/101.10.10.1/32.

That depends on link-security-control on the macsec-entity, which controls the link security policy for handling data packets when the MACsec connection is not available. Values are must-secure and should-secure, and the default is must-secure, so by default unsecured traffic is not passed. Set it with `set macsec-entity-<name> [link-security-control <value>]` or on `add macsec-entity-<name> [supporting-facility <value>] [enabled <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>] [link-security-control <value>] [replay-protection <value>] [replay-protection-window <value>]`. enabled is true/false, default true; replay-protection is enable/disable; replay-protection-window is the number of packets in range 0..4294967295, default 0. show also exposes oper-state and negotiated-cipher-suite. Example: add macsec-entity-6-3-3 supporting-facility ethernet-6-3-3.

Set it on the macsec-mka object: `set macsec-mka-<name> [connectivity-association-key <value>] [connectivity-association-key-name <value>] [mka-policy <value>] [psk-lifetime <value>] [psk-expiration-warning <value>] [psk-lifetime-enable <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>]`. connectivity-association-key is the pre-shared Connectivity Association Key and connectivity-association-key-name its name, both strings of length 0..64. Which end is key server is read from is-key-server, values true/false with default false, via `show macsec-mka-<name> [is-key-server] ...`. psk lifetime/expiration warning is range 1..173 with default 14 days, and psk-lifetime-enable is enabled/disabled. Example: set macsec-mka-6-3-3 connectivity-association-key 1122334411223344556677889900112233445566778899001122334455667788 connectivity-association-key-name aa.

On the mka-policy object, which is the MACsec Key Agreement policy referenced by the macsec entity related to the ethernet facility: `add mka-policy-<name> [key-server-priority <value>] [macsec-cipher-suite <value>] [confidentiality-offset <value>] [sak-rekey-interval <value>]`, with matching set, show and delete. macsec-cipher-suite selects the cipher suite used for Secure Association Key (SAK) derivation. sak-rekey-interval is the SAK re-key interval in seconds, range '0|30..65535', default 30s, so 0 or 30 to 65535. key-server-priority is the priority used by the MKA protocol to select the key server. confidentiality-offset specifies the number of octets in an Ethernet frame that are sent in unencrypted plain-text. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the `re-auth` command, which performs a re-authentication operation of IKEv2 security associations. Syntax: `re-auth [ikev2-peer=]<value>`, where ikev2-peer is a reference to the IKE peer object (IKE SA), given as a string. Access mode: Operational mode. Both the keyword form and the plain AID form work, for example re-auth ikev2-peer=ikev2-NE202 or re-auth ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX2. The scheduled interval is governed separately by re-auth-frequency on the ikev2-peer (3600..604800 seconds, default 43200).

`re-key` performs an on-demand re-key on one of three targets: a data path encryption secure entity, an IKEv2 peer, or an IPsec child security association (Security Policy Database entry). Syntax: `re-key [ipsec-security-association=]<value> | [ikev2-peer=]<value> | [secure-entity=]<value>`. ipsec-security-association points to the IPsec SPD entry object (Child SA), ikev2-peer references the IKE peer object (IKE SA), and secure-entity points to the secure entity object (Child SA); all are strings. Access mode: Operational mode. Examples: re-key secure-entity=NE202-1-4-L1-1 and re-key ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX.

Set the starting port to all and leave the stopping port off: `add remote-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>`, for example add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/all. start accepts all, opaque or a port number; stop is a port-number and, if not set, the system assumes the value 0, which is only accepted when start is set to all or opaque. Only add, show and delete exist since start and stop are part of the key. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. A single port is given as start=stop, e.g. add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/49/49.

Add a remote-subnet under the traffic selector: `add remote-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>`, with matching show and delete. prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, and broadcast for IPv4 only) and is part of the instance key, so there is no set; change it by deleting and re-adding. The parents are the IKEv2 local instance name and peer name (string 1..64, pattern ([A-Za-z0-9 \-.,]*)), the SPD entry name (string 1..32) and the traffic selector name (string 1..64). Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add remote-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/102.20.20.2/32.
